t: You're on the Portman Estate, 110 acres of Marylebone in the West End. The land was first leased to Sir William Portman in 1532, and the estate takes its name from him. Two people are recorded as having died here. Thomas Gibson-Carmichael, Lord Carmichael, was a Scottish Liberal politician, colonial administrator and keen naturalist. Francis Perceval Eliot was an English soldier, auditor and man of letters, who in 1814 inherited the title of Count Eliot but felt it improper to use it.
